body.text: Why do most "free" travel planners and agencies take hidden commissions?

Most "free" travel planners in Türkiye earn their income through supplier kickbacks, wholesale hotel markups, and shopping-stop commissions rather than direct client fees. When an agency waives planning charges, its financial incentive shifts toward properties and operators paying the highest margins—not the hotels, guides, or routes that best fit your trip.

In Türkiye, any company legally operating as a travel agency must be registered with [TÜRSAB (Association of Turkish Travel Agencies)](https://www.tursab.org.tr/about-us) under Law No. 1618. While registration establishes legal standing, the standard commercial model still relies on net-rate markups of 15% to 30% on hotels, private transfers, and domestic packages. On guided days, some low-margin operators also route groups through leather factories, pottery showrooms, or carpet workshops that pay referral percentages.

Even when a bundled quote looks convenient, you rarely see what each hotel, transfer, or licensed guide actually costs. If a boutique cave hotel in Ürgüp refuses to pay high agency rebates, a commission-driven planner simply omits it from your options.
How does Itinerary of Türkiye's flat planning fee model work?

Itinerary of Türkiye operates on a strict client-paid model: Paid by our clients. Independent of provider commissions. Before any planning work starts, our two founders scope your trip complexity and quote a single flat advisory fee in writing, kept completely separate from what you pay airlines, hotels, or local operators.

We call this The ITO Standard—detailed on our [About page](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/about). Because our revenue comes solely from your agreed planning fee, we never accept hotel overrides, restaurant kickbacks, or retail referral payouts. You book directly with vetted providers or through licensed [TÜRSAB-registered agencies](https://www.tursab.org.tr/agency-search) when Turkish law requires an agency-issued package, always seeing the real invoice price.

body.text: What is included in a written ITO plan and provider check?

A written Itinerary of Türkiye plan delivers a day-by-day operational blueprint—not a recycled brochure—paired with independent verification of every hotel, transfer company, and licensed guide before you pay a deposit. You receive realistic drive times, seasonal routing logic, and direct booking links you control.

Every engagement is tailored to your dates—whether a summer coastal loop or a quiet off-season route like our [Türkiye in winter travel guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide). A standard ITO written plan and provider check covers:

items: Route architecture and pacing: Flight pairings, regional transfer buffers, and realistic sightseeing order across Istanbul, Cappadocia, the Aegean, and the Mediterranean.
Shortlisted stays with plain pros and cons: Neighbourhood-level analysis explaining street noise, slope, breakfast quality, and room categories without promotional fluff.

Provider and licence verification: Checking local operator credentials on the [TÜRSAB agency directory](https://www.tursab.org.tr/agency-search), confirming guide licensing, and reviewing cancellation terms before you commit.
Seasonal and operational checks: Aligning museum closures, public holidays, and regional weather windows referenced via [GoTürkiye](https://goturkiye.com/) so your schedule holds up on the ground.
Dining and practical notes: Unpaid local restaurant picks, neighbourhood breakfast spots, and honest cost ranges in current Turkish lira and euro bands.

body.text: Who benefits most from independent local coordination?

Independent local coordination delivers the highest value for travellers planning multi-region Türkiye trips of 7 to 21 days who want insider accuracy without surrendering control to a packaged tour. Families, repeat visitors, and time-poor professionals save dozens of research hours while avoiding costly routing mistakes and inflated agency bundles.

If you are spending a single weekend in Sultanahmet and only need one hotel, you can book that yourself. Flat-fee advisory earns its keep when logistics interlock: pairing an early Cappadocia balloon window with a same-day flight to İzmir, choosing between Kaş and Bodrum for late September, or vetting a private driver for Eastern Anatolia.
